comment: The draft rightly notes SNOMED CT licensing, and SGI covers release management. However, it nowhere states as a requirement that all participating systems must operate on the same versions of the same code systems and value sets. Divergent versions allow one code to carry a changed or deprecated meaning across systems — undermining precisely the semantic consistency the architecture exists to provide.

public.text: The draft rightly notes SNOMED CT licensing, and SGI covers release management. However, it nowhere states as a requirement that all participating systems must operate on the same versions of the same code systems and value sets. Divergent versions allow one code to carry a changed or deprecated meaning across systems — undermining precisely the semantic consistency the architecture exists to provide.
public.suggestedRevision: State explicitly (in §2.2.2 and in the SGI capability categories) that version alignment of terminologies and value sets across all consuming systems is a conformance requirement, with coordinated national release windows, deprecation notice periods, and migration testing as SGI-governed processes.
